method: Rodríguez-Ridao 2020 read in full text on PMC (PMC7579505); Schoenfeld 2017 title confirmed by search; Schoenfeld 2016, ACSM 2009 and Helms 2016 from their published records (seed sources in content/plan.json).

claims.claim: In a 2020 Spanish EMG study of the bench press at five inclinations, a 30 degree incline gave the highest upper (clavicular) pectoralis activity, and steeper inclines shifted work to the anterior deltoid.
claims.source_title: Effect of Five Bench Inclinations on the Electromyographic Activity of the Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid, and Triceps Brachii during the Bench Press Exercise
claims.authors: Rodríguez-Ridao D, Antequera-Vique JA, Martín-Fuentes I, Muyor JM
claims.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339
claims.study_type: Cross-sectional EMG study: 30 resistance-trained adults (University of Almería), free-weight barbell bench press at 0, 15, 30, 45 and 60 degrees, 60% 1RM, 8 reps
claims.finding: Upper pectoralis %MVIC highest at 30 degrees (about 30%), lower at 60 degrees; middle and lower pectoralis fell as incline rose; anterior deltoid rose with incline, highest at 60 degrees. Measured muscle activity, not growth; free-weight bench, not a machine.
claims.on_screen: «على البنش» and «نشاط» in the narration; the caption says it measured activity, not growth.

claims.claim: About 10 or more weekly sets per muscle gave more growth than fewer sets.
claims.source_title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: A systematic review and meta-analysis
claims.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
claims.finding: Graded dose-response; 10+ weekly sets per muscle gave larger gains than fewer than 5.

claims.claim: Training a muscle at least twice a week gave more growth than once a week.
claims.source_title: Effects of Resistance Training Frequency on Measures of Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
claims.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
claims.finding: Twice a week superior to once a week for hypertrophy when volume is equated or not.

claims.claim: Beginners: 8-12 repetitions; increase the load by about 2-10% when the top of the range is exceeded.
claims.source_title: American College of Sports Medicine position stand. Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
claims.finding: 8-12 RM for novices; 2-10% load increase when 1-2 reps over the target can be done.

claims.claim: Choose a load that leaves about 2-3 repetitions in reserve (practical guidance).
claims.source_title: Application of the Repetitions in Reserve-Based Rating of Perceived Exertion Scale for Resistance Training
claims.authors: Helms ER, Cronin J, Storey A, Zourdos MC
claims.finding: RIR-based RPE scale for setting and adjusting load; presented as practical guidance, not a trial result.
